[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve **brackets** first: 37 + 19 = 56.

Multiply: 56 × 2 = 112.

Group all positive and negative numbers: (66 + 28 + 112) − (33 + 49).

Combine: 206 − 82 = 124.

**∴ The correct answer is 124.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 66 + 28 − 33 + (37 + 19) × 2 − 49

To solve this expression, we apply the **BODMAS rule** (Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction) in sequence.

⇒ 66 + 28 − 33 + (56) × 2 − 49

⇒ 66 + 28 − 33 + 112 − 49

⇒ 94 − 33 + 112 − 49

⇒ 61 + 112 − 49

⇒ 173 − 49

⇒ 124

**∴ The correct answer is 124.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It is a standard rule to solve mathematical expressions. Operations must follow the order: **Brackets** (), **Orders** (powers/roots), **Division** (÷), **Multiplication** (×), **Addition** (+), and **Subtraction** (−).

Signs for Operations

When adding or subtracting, always group terms with the same sign together to minimize errors. For example, a − b + c − d can be solved as (a + c) − (b + d).

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Follow **BODMAS**: Solve **Bracket** (29 ÷ 1 = 29) and **Multiplication** (24 × 1 = 24).

Expression simplifies to: 73 + 24 + 29 − 17 + 46 − 26.

Group positive and negative terms: (73 + 24 + 29 + 46) − (17 + 26).

Result: 172 − 43 = 129.

**∴ The correct answer is 129.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given expression: 73 + 24 × 1 + (29 ÷ 1) − 17 + 46 − 26

Step-by-step calculation using **BODMAS** (Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction):

⇒ 73 + 24 × 1 + 29 − 17 + 46 − 26 (Solving **Bracket**)

⇒ 73 + 24 + 29 − 17 + 46 − 26 (Solving **Multiplication**)

⇒ 97 + 29 − 17 + 46 − 26 (Solving **Addition**)

⇒ 126 − 17 + 46 − 26

⇒ 109 + 46 − 26

⇒ 155 − 26 (Solving **Subtraction**)

⇒ 129

**∴ The correct answer is 129.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

The rule defines the correct order of operations: **Brackets** (), **Orders** (powers/roots), **Division** (÷), **Multiplication** (×), **Addition** (+), and **Subtraction** (−).

Identity Property

The **Multiplicative Identity** states that any number multiplied by **1** remains the same (a × 1 = a). Similarly, any number divided by 1 remains unchanged.

Grouping Terms

For faster calculation, all positive values can be summed together and all negative values can be summed together before performing the final **subtraction**.

questions.question: Three bells ring together at 3:00 PM. They ring at intervals of 18 minutes, 24 minutes, and 32 minutes. After how much time will they ring together again?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the next time bells ring together, calculate the **LCM** of the given intervals: 18, 24, and 32.

**LCM**(18, 24, 32) = 288 minutes.

Convert 288 minutes into hours: 288 ÷ 60 = **4 hours 48 minutes**.

Add this duration to the starting time: 3:00 PM + 4:48 = **7:48 PM**.

**∴ The correct answer is 7:48 PM.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Start time = **3:00 PM**

Intervals = **18 minutes**, **24 minutes**, and **32 minutes**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4072a64b65f88a74963f1b5b87af1468475053fb508c002965e76d9d19a2b10d.png] 

Find the **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of the three intervals using prime factorization:

⇒ 18 = 2 × 3²

⇒ 24 = 2³ × 3

⇒ 32 = 2⁵

⇒ LCM = Highest power of each prime factor = 2⁵ × 3²

⇒ LCM = 32 × 9 = **288 minutes**.

Now, convert the total minutes into hours and minutes:

⇒ Hours = 288 ÷ 60 = 4 hours and 48 minutes.

Add this duration to the initial time (3:00 PM):

⇒ 3:00 PM + 4 hours = 7:00 PM

⇒ 7:00 PM + 48 minutes = 7:48 PM.

**∴ The correct answer is 7:48 PM.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The smallest positive integer that is divisible by each of the given numbers. It is used to find recurring meeting points for items with different cycle lengths.

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

The greatest number that divides two or more numbers without a remainder. It is useful for finding the largest possible size of a container or length that fits exactly.

Time Conversion Rules

1 hour = 60 minutes. To convert minutes to hours, divide by 60; the quotient is hours and the remainder is minutes.

questions.question: Two buses leave a station at the same time. Bus A returns every 48 minutes and Bus B returns every 72 minutes. After how many hours will both buses return together at the station for the first time?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ To find when both buses meet for the first time, calculate the **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of their return intervals. **LCM** of 48 and 72 ⇒ 24 × (2, 3) ⇒ 24 × 6 = 144 minutes. Convert 144 minutes to hours: 144 ÷ 60 = 2 hours and 24 minutes. **∴ The correct answer is 2 hr 24 min.**

questions.question: Which of the following is the largest?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For fractions with the **same difference** between numerator and denominator (gap = 1), the one with **larger digits** is greater: 11/12 > 7/8 > 5/6.

Compare the largest from this group (11/12) with the remaining fraction (17/20) using **cross-multiplication**.

11 × 20 = 220 and 12 × 17 = 204.

Since 220 > 204, 11/12 is the **largest fraction** among all given options.

**∴ The correct answer is 11/12.**

Multiply the non-zero numbers: 3 × 4 = 12.

Count the total **decimal places**: 0.003 has 3 places and 0.04 has 2 places (Total = 5).

Place the decimal point 5 positions from the right of 12 (filling with zeros): 0.00012.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.00012.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First number = 0.003

Second number = 0.04

**Method:** Conversion to **fractions**.

⇒ 0.003 = 3 ÷ 1000

⇒ 0.04 = 4 ÷ 100

⇒ Product = (3 ÷ 1000) × (4 ÷ 100)

⇒ Product = (3 × 4) ÷ (1000 × 100)

⇒ Product = 12 ÷ 100000

⇒ Product = 0.00012

**∴ The correct answer is 0.00012.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Multiplication of Decimals

The number of digits after the decimal in the **product** is equal to the sum of the number of digits after the decimal in each factor.

Powers of Ten

Multiplying a decimal by 10−ⁿ shifts the decimal point **n** places to the left (e.g., 12 × 10−⁵ = 0.00012).

Scientific Notation

The value 0.00012 can be expressed as 1.2 × 10−⁴ in standard **scientific notation**.

questions.question: What is the value of sqrt{8 + 2sqrt{15}} ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To simplify a surd of the form **√(A + 2√B)**, identify two numbers whose **sum** is **A** and **product** is **B**.

Here, **A = 8** and **B = 15**. The numbers are **5** and **3** since **5 + 3 = 8** and **5 × 3 = 15**.

The simplified square root is simply **√5 + √3**.

**∴ The correct answer is √3 + √5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Expression:** √(8 + 2√15)

**Formula Used:** (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

⇒ 8 + 2√15 = (5 + 3) + 2√(5 × 3)

⇒ 8 + 2√15 = (√5)² + (√3)² + 2 × √5 × √3

⇒ 8 + 2√15 = (√5 + √3)²

⇒ √(8 + 2√15) = √(√5 + √3)²

⇒ √5 + √3

**∴ The correct answer is √3 + √5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Square Root of Surds

For any expression in the form **√(x ± 2√y)**, if **x = a + b** and **y = ab**, then the simplified value is **√a ± √b**.

Perfect Square Identity

This method relies on the **algebraic identity** **(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²**, which allows us to convert the radicand into a perfect square.

Conjugate Surds

The **conjugate** of a surd **√a + √b** is **√a − √b**. Their product is always a **rational number** **(a − b)**.

questions.question: sqrt{(42 + 31)² - 4 times 42 times 31} = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **algebraic identity**: (a + b)² − 4ab = (a − b)².

Let **a = 42** and **b = 31**.

The expression simplifies to √((42 − 31)²) = 42 − 31.

Result = 11.

**∴ The correct answer is 11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given expression:** √((42 + 31)² − 4 × 42 × 31)

**Method:** Step-by-step simplification using arithmetic operations.

⇒ √((73)² − 4 × 42 × 31)

⇒ √(5329 − 168 × 31)

⇒ √(5329 − 5208)

⇒ √121

⇒ 11

**∴ The correct answer is 11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Important Algebraic Identities

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab and (a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab. The relationship **(a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab** is frequently used in simplification.

Perfect Squares and Square Roots

Memorizing squares up to 30 (e.g., **11² = 121**, 12² = 144) significantly reduces calculation time in **quantitative aptitude** exams.

questions.question: The area of a square is 49 square cm. What is the perimeter (in cm) of the square?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Direct formula: **Perimeter** = 4 × √**Area** Given **Area** = 49 cm² ⇒ **Perimeter** = 4 × √49 ⇒ **Perimeter** = 4 × 7 = 28 cm **∴ The correct answer is 28 cm.**

questions.question: The area of a square is 121 square cm. What is the side (in cm) of the square?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **side** of a **square** is the **square root** of its **area**.

**Side** = √121 = **11 cm**

**∴ The correct answer is 11 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Area** of the **square** = 121 cm²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/76937d52ed5fb87db4b43707c332fff6a21ab019a3e3dc8fc09e880eb19388d6.png] 

**Formula Used:**

**Area** of a **square** = (**side**)²

**Calculations:**

⇒ 121 = (**side**)²

⇒ **side** = √121

⇒ **side** = 11 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 11 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perimeter of a Square

The total boundary length or **perimeter** is calculated as 4 × **side**.

Diagonal of a Square

The **diagonal** of a **square** with **side** 's' is given by the formula s × √2.

Area using Diagonal

If the **diagonal** 'd' is given, the **area** can also be found using (d²) ÷ 2.

questions.question: 1³ + 2³ + 3³ + ... + 25³ = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **sum of the cubes of first n natural numbers** is given by the formula [n(n+1)/2]².

For n = 25, the sum is [25 × (25 + 1) / 2]².

Sum = [25 × 13]² = 325².

Shortcut for 325²: 32 × 33 = 1056, then suffix 25 → 105625.

**∴ The correct answer is 105625.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Series = 1³ + 2³ + 3³ + ... + 25³

Total number of terms (n) = 25

**Formula Used:**

Sum of cubes of first n natural numbers (Sₙ) = [n(n + 1) / 2]²

**Calculations:**

⇒ S₂₅ = [25 × (25 + 1) / 2]²

⇒ S₂₅ = [25 × 26 / 2]²

⇒ S₂₅ = [25 × 13]²

⇒ S₂₅ = 325²

⇒ S₂₅ = 325 × 325

⇒ S₂₅ = 105625

**∴ The correct answer is 105625.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of first n natural numbers

The sum of the first n natural numbers (1 + 2 + ... + n) is given by the formula Sₙ = n(n + 1) / 2.

Sum of squares of first n natural numbers

The sum of the squares (1² + 2² + ... + n²) is given by the formula Sₙ = n(n + 1)(2n + 1) / 6.

Relation between sum of numbers and sum of cubes

The sum of the cubes of the first n natural numbers is always the square of the sum of the first n natural numbers.

questions.question: Average age of a group of 16 boys is 22 years. Two boys with ages 20 years and 21 years left the group. One boy with age 34 years joined the group. What is the new average age (in years) of the group?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Initial **Total Age** = 16 × 22 = 352 years **Net Change** in age = 34 (joined) − 20 (left) − 21 (left) = −7 years New **Total Age** = 352 − 7 = 345 years New **Total Boys** = 16 − 2 + 1 = 15 boys New **Average Age** = 345 ÷ 15 = 23 years **∴ The correct answer is 23 years.**

questions.question: A person sells an article at the profit of 40 percent. Cost price and selling price are increased by 25 percent and 'y' percent respectively. If the new profit percentage is 20 percent, then what is the value of 'y'?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume initial **Cost Price (CP)** = 100 ⇒ initial **Selling Price (SP)** = 140.

New **CP** = 100 + 25% = 125.

New **SP** at 20% profit = 125 × 1.2 = 150.

The value of **y** is the percentage increase in **SP**: [(150 − 140) ÷ 140] × 100 = 7.14.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.14.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/caadac12ba018d1ef6ff1434419112d3384cda6b7351c4da8a6917df8e1c9e68.png] 

**Given:** Initial Profit% = 40%, **CP increase** = 25%, **New Profit%** = 20%.

**Formula:** Selling Price (SP) = CP × (1 + Profit/100).

⇒ Let **Initial Cost Price (CP₁)** = 100.

⇒ **Initial Selling Price (SP₁)** = 100 × (1 + 40/100) = 140.

⇒ **New Cost Price (CP₂)** = 100 × (1 + 25/100) = 125.

⇒ **New Selling Price (SP₂)** = 125 × (1 + 20/100) = 125 × 1.2 = 150.

⇒ Increase in **SP** = SP₂ − SP₁ = 150 − 140 = 10.

⇒ **y** = (Increase / Original SP) × 100 = (10 / 140) × 100.

⇒ **y** = 100 ÷ 14 ≈ 7.14.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.14.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit Percentage Formula

Profit% is always calculated on the **Cost Price (CP)** unless stated otherwise. Formula: [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100.

Percentage Change in Variables

When multiple variables (CP and Profit%) change, the new **Selling Price** is found by applying the new profit percentage to the updated base CP.

Successive Percentage

The effective change in **SP** depends on the base shift of **CP** and the change in the **profit margin**. Use the unitary method for faster comparisons.

questions.question: Cost price of 35 articles is Rs. 208. Selling price of 40 articles is Rs. 208. What is the ratio of the value of profit/loss of 1 article to the selling price of 1 article? (Cost price of all the articles is same. Selling price of all the articles is same.)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If **Cost Price (CP)** of **x** items = **Selling Price (SP)** of **y** items, then the ratio **CP/SP = y/x**.

Here, x = 35 and y = 40 ⇒ CP/SP = 40/35 = 8/7.

Let **CP** = 8 units and **SP** = 7 units.

**Loss** = CP − SP = 8 − 7 = 1 unit.

Required Ratio = **Loss** : **SP** = 1 : 7.

**∴ The correct answer is 1:7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total **Cost Price** of 35 articles = ₹208

Total **Selling Price** of 40 articles = ₹208

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/025f8b0683911f59fb4be1e18a34ccb36b72e695d3fae7237ac2065ee9e8174d.png] 

**Formula Used:**

**Loss** = CP − SP

**Ratio** = (Loss per article) : (SP per article)

**Calculations:**

⇒ **CP** of 1 article (CP₁) = 208 ÷ 35

⇒ **SP** of 1 article (SP₁) = 208 ÷ 40

⇒ Since CP₁ > SP₁, it is a **Loss**.

⇒ **Loss** per article = CP₁ − SP₁ = (208 ÷ 35) − (208 ÷ 40)

⇒ Ratio = (CP₁ − SP₁) ÷ SP₁

⇒ Ratio = (CP₁ ÷ SP₁) − 1

⇒ Ratio = [(208 ÷ 35) ÷ (208 ÷ 40)] − 1

⇒ Ratio = (40 ÷ 35) − 1 = (8 ÷ 7) − 1

⇒ Ratio = 1 ÷ 7 = 1 : 7

**∴ The correct answer is 1:7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basics

**Profit** occurs when SP > CP (Profit = SP − CP). **Loss** occurs when CP > SP (Loss = CP − SP).

The CP and SP Relation

When the total value of CP for x items equals the total value of SP for y items, the per-unit price ratio is inversely proportional to the quantities: **CP₁/SP₁ = y/x**.

Percentage Loss/Profit

Percentage is always calculated on the **Cost Price**: Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

questions.question: Out of two numbers, 25 percent of the smaller number is equal to 10 percent of the larger number. If the sum of both the numbers is 2380, then what is the value of the larger number?
questions.solution:

The ratio of the numbers is the inverse of their percentage coefficients.

**Smaller number** : **Larger number** = 10% : 25% = 2 : 5

Total units = 2 + 5 = 7 units

7 units = 2380 ⇒ 1 unit = 340

**Larger number** = 5 units = 5 × 340 = 1700

**∴ The correct answer is 1700.**

questions.question: M alone can complete a work in 45 days. N alone can complete the same work in 90 days. Both of them work together. In 10 days what percent work of the total work will be completed?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Combined efficiency of **M** and **N** = (1/45) + (1/90) = 3/90 = 1/30 work per day.

Work done in **10 days** = 10 × (1/30) = 1/3 of the total work.

Work percentage = (1/3) × 100 = **33.33%**.

**∴ The correct answer is 33.33%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given that **M** completes work in **45 days** and **N** completes it in **90 days**.

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work (LCM)**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 M
 45
 90 units
 2 units/day
 
 

 N
 90
 1 unit/day
 
 

⇒ Total efficiency of (M + N) = 2 + 1 = **3 units/day**.

⇒ Work completed in **10 days** = 3 units/day × 10 days = **30 units**.

⇒ Percent of work completed = (Work Done ÷ Total Work) × 100

⇒ Percent of work completed = (30 ÷ 90) × 100

⇒ Percent of work completed = (1 ÷ 3) × 100 = **33.33%**.

**∴ The correct answer is 33.33%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a work. Efficiency = 1 ÷ Time.

Combined Work Formula

If A takes 'x' days and B takes 'y' days, together they take (x × y) ÷ (x + y) days to finish the work.

Remaining Work

Remaining Work = 1 − (Work Completed). In percentage, it is 100% − (Percentage of work completed).

questions.question: The speed of stream is 5 km/hr. A boat goes 90 km upstream and comes back to the starting point in 24 hours. What is the speed (in km/hr) of the boat in still water?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **option substitution method** in the time equation: 90/(u − 5) + 90/(u + 5) = 24.

Test **u = 10 km/hr** from the options.

Time = (90/5) + (90/15) ⇒ 18 + 6 = 24 **hours**.

The total time matches the given 24 hours perfectly.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Speed of stream** (v) = 5 km/hr

**Total distance** (one way) = 90 km

**Total time taken** = 24 hr

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Upstream Speed = (u − v) | Downstream Speed = (u + v)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/524333f31a376cf25f8c0d1136b87999e53f6f11181f0211f6fa4925762dc133.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 90/(u − 5) + 90/(u + 5) = 24

⇒ 15/(u − 5) + 15/(u + 5) = 4 (Dividing by 6)

⇒ 15 × [(u + 5 + u − 5) / (u² − 25)] = 4

⇒ 15 × (2u) = 4(u² − 25)

⇒ 30u = 4u² − 100

⇒ 4u² − 30u − 100 = 0

⇒ 2u² − 15u − 50 = 0

⇒ 2u² − 20u + 5u − 50 = 0

⇒ 2u(u − 10) + 5(u − 10) = 0

⇒ (2u + 5)(u − 10) = 0

⇒ u = 10 (as speed cannot be negative)

**∴ The correct answer is 10 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Downstream Speed (D)

It is the net speed when a boat travels in the direction of the stream: D = u + v.

Upstream Speed (U)

It is the net speed when a boat travels against the direction of the stream: U = u − v.

Speed in Still Water (u)

The speed of the boat without the stream factor: u = (D + U) ÷ 2.

Speed of Stream (v)

The rate at which the water flows: v = (D − U) ÷ 2.

questions.question: On selling an article at (13/15) of the marked price there is a profit of 30 percent. What will be the ratio of marked price of the article to its cost price of the article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **Marked Price (MP)** of the article be 15 units.

**Selling Price (SP)** = (13/15) × 15 = 13 units.

Given **Profit** is 30%, it means **SP** = 130% of **Cost Price (CP)**.

⇒ 130% of CP = 13 units ⇒ 100% of CP = (13 ÷ 130) × 100 = 10 units.

Required **Ratio** (MP : CP) = 15 : 10 = 3 : 2.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 2.**

questions.question: The marked price of an article is Rs. 2000. It is sold at a discount of 10 percent. The profit percentage is 60 percent. What is the cost price of the article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the direct ratio formula: **CP/MP = (100 − Discount%)/(100 + Profit%)**

CP/2000 = (100 − 10)/(100 + 60)

CP/2000 = 90/160 = 9/16

CP = (9/16) × 2000 = 9 × 125 = 1125

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1125.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Marked Price (MP)** = Rs. 2000

**Discount** = 10%

**Profit** = 60%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cc699c84449737dda81860c010b64104452ae402d15ac80507279c973d3ba990.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = MP − Discount

⇒ SP = 2000 − (10% of 2000)

⇒ SP = 2000 − 200 = Rs. 1800

⇒ **Cost Price (CP)** = SP × 100/(100 + Profit%)

⇒ CP = 1800 × 100/(100 + 60)

⇒ CP = 1800 × 100/160

⇒ CP = 1800 × 5/8

⇒ CP = 225 × 5 = Rs. 1125

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1125.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relationship between CP and MP

The ratio of Cost Price to Marked Price is always CP/MP = (100 − D%)/(100 + P%), where D is discount and P is profit.

Markup Percentage

Markup % = (MP − CP)/CP × 100. It represents how much the price is increased above the cost price.

Successive Discounts

Two successive discounts of d₁% and d₂% are equivalent to a single discount of [d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂)/100]%.
